notes: In-universe news (sites.legitreal.com) as attributed, verbatim-verified claims. Claims are quoted as reports, never upgraded to unattributed fact.

seed_sources.name: MOUK campaign brief
seed_sources.attribution: The Medical Officers Union of Kingstonia
seed_sources.note: Partisan client brief. Use only with attribution; single-source items stay attributed until news corroborates them.

claims.statement: a poll shows Yes on 35.2%, No on 35.2% and 29% unsure
Kingstonia Central Hospital has forty empty nursing posts
the first H2D2 vaccine shipment is due to land in about a fortnight
the referendum vote is on 2 November
President Hawthorne is voting Yes and roughly half his party is voting with him
Marina Castillo called the referendum a power grab in a lab coat on Kingstonia Tonight

counter_cards.concern: A proof requirement creates a two-tier society.
counter_cards.fair_part: Rules that limit access do burden people who cannot or will not comply, and that deserves an honest answer.
counter_cards.response: There is one hospital system, and it is already forty nurses short; an entry rule is about keeping that one system working for everyone, including people who cannot be vaccinated.
avoid: Do not say the hospital is full; the reported fact is forty nurse vacancies.

counter_cards.concern: Employers and tourism businesses say they cannot afford it.
counter_cards.fair_part: Checks add work for small businesses, and the last pandemic hurt tourism badly.
counter_cards.response: The expensive outcome is another outbreak and another closure; a clear rule now is cheaper than shutting doors later.

counter_cards.concern: The mandate is a power grab in a lab coat.
counter_cards.fair_part: Emergency powers can be abused, and people are right to ask how long a rule lasts.
counter_cards.response: This is a public referendum, not an emergency decree; voters decide, and the government has said it will respect the result.
avoid: Do not attack Marina Castillo personally.
Do not claim details about a sunset clause that have not been published.

counter_cards.concern: The new national ID could become a health passport that tracks people.
counter_cards.fair_part: Privacy questions about linking health data to ID cards are legitimate and still being debated.
counter_cards.response: Supporting proof at entry does not require backing every possible data system; ask for clear limits on what is stored and who can see it.
avoid: Do not claim how the ID system will work; that is not settled.
